[Interview, 2010-12-02, Talk of the Nation]
HOST: Thank you very much, Jason.
GUEST: So Tony...

HOST: Go ahead.
GUEST: So Tony, can I ask him a question.

HOST: He's gone, unfortunately.
GUEST: Okay. Well, here's my rhetorical question. You know, when was the last time look, when I quit the Lexington-Herald Leader, I didn't get an opportunity to have my many gifted sponsors, you know, give money to charities that I thought that mattered. You know, when I quit, I just chucked the duece(ph) and headed for the door. You know - I mean? Everybody is talking about the way that he did it. How would you have done it? I mean, what is the best he didn't do a Steven Slater. He didn't grave a beer, hope on the plane and just get out. I mean, how would you have done it? What was the best way for him to do it? I mean, listen, this was a tough decision that I wouldn't wish on a goat. You know, this young man, all things considered, you know, he handled this as well as anybody could be expected to handle it. I'm sorry.

HOST: I'm sure there are a lot of people that are not going to agree with you on that. I'm going to take...
GUEST: Of course.

HOST: ...the chalk, and sprays it into the air. Do you think he would have the nerve to do that tonight?
GUEST: Why not?

HOST: Because...
GUEST: Why shouldn't he do it, Tony?

HOST: Here's an email from Michael in Tucson. He says, LeBron's long-term financial success, to your point, GUEST, is based on fan appreciation. Clearly, the fans' reaction to LeBron's leaving shows that the way he left was a mistake. Another question for you is this: The Miami Heat the he is now on - I think they're 11-8. They won last night by 25 points. They're not doing so well. Are people sort of like, in Cleveland, feeling, okay, good, you're getting yours back?
GUEST: I think there's a sense that he got to warm up, you know? You can't just come up on a team and all of a sudden you guys are in the winner's circle. I mean, everybody has to kind of get to know each other and get to know each other - how they play. So I mean, time will tell if he made the right decision or not.
